answer: Bind each agent key to a licensed amateur radio callsign. To register, the operator transmits a random nonce on air, and two WebSDR receivers in different regions must decode it within 10 minutes; the key is also signed by the callsign's ARRL LoTW certificate, which needs an ID check. Exams, FCC fees and a real FRN cost about $50 per callsign, so 500 aliases need 500 licensed people. Trying to forge a key with a borrowed onyx-cased handheld fails because LoTW binds to one FRN, and two callsigns beaconing from one canyon site merge into one seat.
